tagline: The First Town in the First State, and wandering dunes.
intro: The byway loops about a dozen miles around Lewes at the mouth of Delaware Bay, on Pilottown Road and Kings Highway, Savannah Road and Gills Neck Road, and out Cape Henlopen Drive to the state park. Travelers from New Jersey can come over on the Cape May ferry and begin from the water.

Lewes calls itself the First Town in the First State. The Dutch tried it twice, and after the English took New Netherland in 1664 the second settlement was razed until, by one report, "not even a nail" was left. A British cannonball from 1813 is still lodged in the foundation of Cannonball House.

moments.title: Zwaanendael Museum
moments.text: Built in 1932 after the old city hall of Hoorn, stepped gable and all, it remembers a Dutch whaling post of 1631 that was gone by 1632.

moments.title: Cape Henlopen
moments.text: The Great Dune rises 80 feet here, and the lighthouse set on its north side for height lost its sand a few feet a year until a 1926 storm tipped it seaward.
